nonclaims: external novelty or priority for the classical recurrent sandpile and critical-group facts
prime semantics for critical-group translations or their repetitions
permutation or unitarity of addition-stabilization on all stable configurations
a target divisor, functional equation, counting law, continuation, or Weil compression
arithmetic local factors, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, a Hilbert--Polya operator, Route-B authorization, or external peer review

orbit_spectral_theorem.cycles: every recurrent orbit has exact length L and there are D/L primitive cycles
orbit_spectral_theorem.fixed_counts: #Fix(T_b^n on recurrent configurations)=D if L divides n and zero otherwise
orbit_spectral_theorem.reversal: group inversion R is involutive and R*T_b*R=T_b^(-1); conjugation after R is antiunitary
orbit_spectral_theorem.self_adjoint: the finite Koopman unitary U_b is self-adjoint if and only if L<=2
orbit_spectral_theorem.spectrum: every L-th root of unity occurs with multiplicity D/L

order_theorem.definition: L=ord_K([b])=min{ell>=1: ell*b lies in Delta Z^(V_non_sink)}
order_theorem.sink_only: if r=0, use D=L=1 and the singleton empty recurrent configuration

progress_and_boundary.progress: proves the all-graph recurrent-torsor bridge, two exact translation-order formulas, uniform orbit law, zeta, determinant, spectrum, reversal and self-adjoint boundary
progress_and_boundary.route_a_obstruction: the exact critical-group dynamics has no intrinsic prime semantics, target divisor comparison, or target global analytic structure
progress_and_boundary.sentinel_boundary: finite simple-graph enumeration regression-tests the proof and does not extrapolate the multigraph theorem

recurrent_bridge_theorem.representatives: every class in K(G,s) has a unique recurrent stable representative, so the recurrent set is a canonical K(G,s)-torsor and has D elements
recurrent_bridge_theorem.scope: the theorem is on recurrent stable configurations; it does not identify all stable configurations with the critical group
recurrent_bridge_theorem.translation: T_b(eta)=stabilize(eta+b) preserves the recurrent set and is translation by [b]

source_lock.allowed_data: the frozen graph, sink, chip vector, reduced Laplacian, recurrent configurations and derived exact group data
source_lock.arithmetic_origin: none; the graph critical group and chip addition have no intrinsic rational-prime or prime-power semantics
source_lock.cutoff: all-graph proof; exhaustive simple-graph regression on all 30 connected isomorphism types with 2<=|V|<=5, every sink, and zero/unit/all-ones additions
source_lock.determinant_convention: Artin--Mazur zeta and finite Koopman determinant of T_b restricted to the recurrent set
source_lock.family: every such graph, every sink, and every nonnegative chip vector b on the non-sink vertices
source_lock.forbidden_data: target zero or prime tables, arithmetic local data, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, Hilbert--Polya operators, and Route-B inputs
source_lock.normalization: stable heights 0<=eta_v<deg(v), reduced Laplacian Delta, uniform counting measure on recurrent configurations
source_lock.object: addition and stabilization on recurrent stable configurations of a finite connected undirected loopless multigraph with a designated sink
source_lock.precision: exact integer topplings, determinants, adjugates, quotient orders and finite permutations

stable_state_boundary.counterexample: on the path 0-1-2 with sink 2 and b=(1,0), both stable states (0,0) and (0,1) map to (0,1), while the recurrent set is the singleton {(0,1)}
stable_state_boundary.nonclaim: no all-stable-state cycle classification or eventual-recurrence theorem is asserted for arbitrary b
stable_state_boundary.warning: addition-stabilization on all stable configurations need not be injective or unitary and is not the phase space of the translation theorem
